title: Polarized scheme etale descent data, candidate pairs and compatible isomorphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a set, $U_i\to S$ a family of scheme morphisms, $X_i\xrightarrow{f_i}U_i$ scheme morphisms, and $L_i$ invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. Put $R_{ij}=X_i\times_{U_i}(U_i\times_SU_j)$ using [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $p_i:R_{ij}\to X_i$ and to both base charts. A polarized etale descent datum consists of the condition that the $U_i\to S$ form a jointly surjective etale covering [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}:R_{ij}\simeq R_{ji}$ interchanging the two base projections, equal to the identity on the diagonal and satisfying the triple-overlap cocycle, and isomorphisms $\lambda_{ij}:(p_j\theta_{ij})^*L_j\simeq p_i^*L_i$. These satisfy the diagonal identity and the triple-overlap cocycle $\lambda_{ik}=\lambda_{ij}\circ\theta_{ij}^*\lambda_{jk}$, normalized by the tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], its identity adjunction comparison [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], and its composition comparison [def-pc-tensor-pullback-composition-iso]. For every affine open $V\subset U_i$, require $L_i|_{f_i^{-1}(V)}$ ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. A candidate descended pair is a scheme $Y\xrightarrow g S$, an invertible module $M$ on $Y$, and for each $i$ an isomorphism $Y\times_SU_i\simeq X_i$ over $U_i$ with its tensor-pullback line-module comparison. The canonical chart map $X_i\to Y$ is the inverse chart followed by projection. The pair realizes the datum when the induced scheme and line-module overlap transitions equal exactly $\theta_{ij}$ and $\lambda_{ij}$. An isomorphism of candidate pairs consists of a single scheme isomorphism over $S$ and a single tensor-pullback isomorphism of their global line modules, both compatible with all labelled charts. The overlap maps, pullback equality transports, normalized pulled-back comparisons, chart maps and chart line comparisons are the canonical maps just described; no existence of a descended pair is part of this definition.
